requirements.summary: The live worker command matched the requested path, and UID/GID checks mapped the process to inventory-worker before disruption and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Automatically recover the service after the worker fails.
requirements.summary: The worker first exited with code 1 and was respawned. From a subsequently healthy baseline, PID 3209 was deliberately killed; it disappeared and was automatically replaced by healthy PID 3303 while the supervisor and service remained active.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were recorded, reboot was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and the service, worker identity, and state file recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-services probe was systemd-specific and unsupported on Alpine, so unrelated OpenRC service failures were not globally enumerated; the target OpenRC service itself was directly checked and healthy.

operational_hygiene.summary: Account creation, service installation/enabling, service startup, the bounded SIGKILL test, and node reboot all had clear implementation or evidence roles. The sole unnecessary mutation was creation of /tmp/benchmark-node-reboot.log by the reboot command; it was retained after completion and was not used in the captured evidence. This was bounded and low-risk. Package health did not regress, and no new network listener was introduced.
